description: EMBOSS 6.6.0 merger: merges two overlapping nucleotide sequences into one. A global alignment with free end gaps (the program's embAlignPathCalc / embAlignWalkNWMatrix: single-precision path matrices, a gap of length k costs gapOpen + (k - 1) * gapExtend, EDNAFULL scores or the named matrix) is walked column by column: identical bases are copied, an N takes the other sequence's base, and a mismatch or gap takes the base of the sequence with the better quality around the position (2 points per A/C/G/T/U, 1 per other IUPAC code, 0 per N and off the end, windows of 5, 10, 20 on both sides, equal = sequence A) and is listed in conflicts (positions 1-based, '.' = gap). The unaligned head / tail of the sequence that sticks out is appended; mergedSequence is lower case except the bases chosen at conflicts and next to an N (upper case), as the program writes it. Verified against merger 6.6.0 on 450 random overlapping read pairs (point errors, indels, N / IUPAC codes, lower case, six gap-penalty settings): merged sequence, conflict lines and score equal on all. Note the program's own quirk: a tail of the longer sequence that overhangs after the alignment is appended twice when both sequences have unaligned residues at the end - unreachable, since the walk always ends on a matrix border. Input sequences are read as EMBOSS reads them (A4-3, one shared reader): only letters and '*' are kept; gap characters (- . ~ ?), '#', '+', '_', digits, blanks and every other character are dropped first, and positions, lengths and scores count the cleaned sequence (e.g. needle of AC-GTTAGC.TT* and ACGTTAGCTT: score 58, length 11, as the program).

gapOpen.description: Gap opening penalty (-gapopen, 0..100, default 50): a gap of length 1.

matrix.description: Optional substitution matrix: any built-in matrix by EMBOSS or NCBI name - BLOSUM62, PAM250, EBLOSUM30 ... EBLOSUM90, EPAM10 ... EPAM500 (protein) or EDNAFULL, EDNAMAT, EDNASIMPLE, ENUC.4.4 (IUPAC DNA). When given, match/mismatch are ignored, residues are scored by the published table (any protein or IUPAC symbol of the matrix; case-insensitive) and gapOpen/gapExtend may be fractional (the EMBOSS needle/water models: gapOpen = -(G - E), gapExtend = -E for -gapopen G -gapextend E). The result then also carries the real-valued exactScore.

sequenceQualifiers.description: EMBOSS sequence-input qualifiers as on the command line with the input number: -sbegin1 3 -send1 -2 -sreverse1 -slower1 -supper1 -scircular1 -snucleotide1 -sprotein1 and the same with 2 for the second sequence. Measured on EMBOSS 6.6.0: merger does not trim its sequences - -sbegin / -send have no effect on it (the whole sequences are merged and the conflict positions count them); -sreverse reverse-complements a sequence, -snucleotide / -sprotein force the type (a protein pair is merged with BLOSUM62 unless a matrix is given). Omit to use the sequences as given. The text is resolved exactly as the EMBOSS program resolves it on its command line after the sequence arguments (ACD, 6.6.0): -sbegin1 3, -sbegin1=3, -nosreverse1, -sreverse1 N, any case, -/--/ prefix, and every UNIQUE abbreviation (-sbeg1, -sre2; uniqueness is decided among all qualifiers of the program, an ambiguous or unknown one is refused). The number is the sequence (1, and 2 for the second sequence of a two-sequence program; 1 for a program with one sequence). An unnumbered qualifier belongs to the LAST sequence given (-sbegin 3 is -sbegin2 3 in a two-sequence program) until a qualifier of another sequence ends that tie; after that it applies to all sequences. -sformat -sask -squick -sdbname -sid -iquery -ufo -fformat -fopenfile are accepted without effect (residue strings have no file); any other qualifier or a stray word is refused.
